name: Legwork
description: Lets an agent find an open-source tool on GitHub and install it as an MCP tool on this machine. find_tools only searches; install_tool clones, scans and builds a repo in an OS sandbox (sandbox-exec on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux); use_tool and the exported <repo>__<tool> tools run it with only the folders and network the user granted. Installs run third-party code with network on. External, opt-in, off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Start the hub with only the folders tools need (--allow-read ~/Downloads, read-only) and without --allow-net; an install can ask for those grants or fewer, never more.
Call install_tool with preview: true first, then with commit set to the full SHA it reports, so the approval names the exact commit that is built.
For a repo not in the Legwork cache, read the model-written install command the build stops to show; none of it runs until that exact text is approved.
Prefer repos find_tools marks as in the Legwork cache: their install command is pinned and reviewed, and each passes a known-answer test.
Pin the package (uvx legwork-mcp==<version>) so only a release you have reviewed runs; legwork show and legwork log print what each tool was built from and what it reached.
